rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-4, nine weighing lysimeters with flood, surface drip and subsurface drip treatments on winter wheat at LAES-CAS, one season 2017-2018. Q2: Table 1 and Section 4.2, grain yield reported for flood (4694.8 kg/ha), surface drip (4428.0) and subsurface drip (4584.8), with flood highest. Q4: Table 2 and Section 4.3 report ET and soil water storage per treatment, and Figure 6 / Section 4.5 report leaf gas exchange (photosynthesis, stomatal conductance, transpiration) as intermediates linking irrigation method to yield.
rows.notes: The study's own result contradicts the direction of the claim: drip (both SDI and SSDI) gave lower grain yield than flood irrigation (statistically different letters in Table 1); authors describe yield as 'similar' for SSDI and flood but it is not an increase. Single site, single crop, single season, lysimeter scale; no SD or CI reported, only means with letter groupings; no stated limitations beyond a future-work remark on partitioning soil and leaf water loss.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-4, lysimeter experiment with FI, SDI and SSDI on winter wheat. Q2: Section 4.1 and Table 2, SSDI total ET 220.96 mm versus 300.30 mm under flood (26% lower, ~80 mm saved) with irrigation input 120 mm versus 190 mm; Table 3 shows higher CWP and IWP under SSDI. Q4: Figure 6 / Section 4.5, lower leaf transpiration rate and stomatal conductance measured under SSDI, and Table 2 soil water storage highest in SSDI, offered as the pathway for reduced ET.
rows.notes: Water saving established by one method (weighing lysimeter mass change feeding the water balance); leaf gas exchange was a one-day measurement and does not independently quantify seasonal water use. Soil evaporation, the mechanism the authors invoke, was not measured directly. The 4,420 million m3/yr regional saving in Section 5.4 is an extrapolation, not a measured result. No dispersion statistics; limitations not stated.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-4, own lysimeter experiment comparing flood, surface drip and subsurface drip for winter wheat.
rows.notes: The study contains no observation or measurement of weeds or weed control; it reports ET, water balance, yield components, water productivity and leaf gas exchange only. No evidence on the pest/weed control claim.

notes: Full text appears complete. Single-season (2017-2018) lysimeter study with three replicates per treatment at one site in the North China Plain; results are means with LSD letter groupings and no standard deviations or intervals.
